---
task: "Deploy LSV Operational Service Summary behind AccessBuddy auth"
slug: 20261116-211000_lsv-service-summary-deploy
project: lsv-service-summary
effort: deep
effort_source: classifier
phase: observe
progress: 0/96
mode: interactive
started: 2026-11-16T10:11:00Z
updated: 2026-11-16T10:40:00Z
---

## Problem

Life Saving Victoria's Operational Service Summary tool lives as a claude.ai artifact: one 130 KB vanilla-JS `index.html` whose storage is claude.ai's artifact store and whose "capabilities" (`window.claude.use("user" | "downloads" | "sample")`) only exist inside claude.ai. That host cannot reach the Bureau of Meteorology, so twice a week a member runs a bookmarklet on bom.gov.au and pastes the result into the Weather tab by hand. The data is behind claude.ai sharing rather than an organisational login, the page cannot be slotted into LIMSOC's interface chooser, and nothing is automated. The tool needs a real home: an authenticated site at a stable URL, a multi-user backend with live updates, and a scheduled job that fills the weather grid without anyone pasting anything.

## Vision

A comms member opens nicholas.wood.com.au/lsv/dailysummary on Tuesday morning, signs in exactly the way they would for AccessBuddy, sees "Welcome Sarah" on a LIMSOC-styled chooser, clicks Service Management, and the Weather tab already holds seven days of BOM figures issued at 05:30 that morning. A colleague editing SC40's hours in another browser appears live. The Word export fills LSV's own template. Nothing about the app itself feels different from the artifact; what changed is that it is now a service rather than a page.

## Out of Scope

- Any change to the app's UI, flows, wording, or document generation beyond what hosting, auth, storage, and weather automation strictly require. The Excel-like simplicity is deliberate.
- Any call to LIMSOC production (limsoc.com.au), for reads or writes, and any new LIMSOC API integration without Nick's explicit approval. Unit data came from staging only.
- Public republication of BOM data. The site stays behind login; no anonymous weather endpoint.
- Paid infrastructure beyond Google Cloud's free tier unless Nick approves it after a cost estimate.
- A second interface-chooser entry, LIMSOC embedding, or SSO with LIMSOC. The chooser keeps the look so it can be slotted in later; the slotting is not this work.
- Mobile app, offline mode, or PWA packaging.
- Rebuilding the page in a framework. Splitting into modules is allowed only with behaviour held identical.

## Principles

- **Same security posture as AccessBuddy, not a lookalike.** Sign-in, session handling, and access checks are the same mechanisms, ideally the same code, so one audit covers both.
- **A member's typed value is sacred.** Automation fills gaps and refreshes its own figures; it never overwrites a human edit.
- **Nothing readable without a session.** Page, data API, and live-update channel all refuse signed-out requests.
- **Infrastructure as code, deploy from a release.** If it is not in Terraform or a workflow, it does not exist.
- **Cost honesty.** Anything outside the free tier is surfaced with an estimate before it is created.
- **Behaviour parity is the regression test.** The artifact is the oracle: exports, imports, and views must match it byte-for-intent.

## Constraints

- Auth: Firebase Auth email magic link, email OTP, and passkeys as in AccessBuddy (`apps/web/src/lib/auth.ts`), producing the `session` cookie (httpOnly, secure, SameSite=Lax, 14 days), validated server-side on every request. No passwords. Dev login only when `NODE_ENV !== production`.
- Hosting: Next.js on Cloud Run, australia-southeast1, Terraform in `infra/terraform`, GitHub Actions CI, release-please gated deploy over Workload Identity Federation, Secret Manager for secrets, Cloud Scheduler for the weather job authenticated with a cron secret header.
- URL: served under the path prefix `/lsv/dailysummary`; the page keeps hash routing (`#home`, `#services`, `#weather`, `#events`, `#report`, `#setup`).
- Storage interface preserved verbatim: `db.collection(name).onSnapshot(cb)` → `{docs:[{id,data()}]}`; `db.doc(path).onSnapshot(cb)` → `{exists,data()}`; `db.doc(path).set(obj)`; `db.doc(path).delete()`. Collections `units`, `events`, `weather`, `confirmations`, `summaries`; docs `config/settings`, `config/contacts`.
- Weather feeds via anonymous FTP only: `ftp://ftp.bom.gov.au/anon/gen/fwo/IDV10753.xml`, `IDV10752.xml`, `IDV10751.xml`, with a descriptive User-Agent. Not the www.bom.gov.au/fwo URLs.
- Wording: "members" never "staff". `unit.area` holds Region (Central/East/West); `unit.regionName` holds Area (Bass, Port Phillip, Kingston, ...).
- Build: changes go into `src/ux/*` parts and `build.py` rebuilds `index.html`; never hand-edit the built file. Library versions pinned: docx@8.5.0, xlsx@0.18.5, jszip@3.10.1.
- Tooling: bun, TypeScript, Terraform; Python only where the pack already uses it (`build.py`, `build_seed.py`).

## Goal

The Operational Service Summary runs at `https://nicholas.wood.com.au/lsv/dailysummary` on Nick's Google Cloud with AccessBuddy's sign-in, session, and access model; its data lives in an authenticated backend seeded from the 2026-11-16 export with live multi-user updates; a twice-daily Cloud Scheduler job fills seven days of BOM weather without overwriting member-typed values; and a README covers deploy, rollback, weather rerun, and restore.

## Criteria

### Auth and session (AccessBuddy parity)
- [ ] ISC-1: `GET /lsv/dailysummary` without a `session` cookie returns a 3xx to the sign-in page (curl -i).
- [ ] ISC-2: `GET /lsv/dailysummary/api/docs/units` without a cookie returns 401 JSON, not data (curl -i).
- [ ] ISC-3: The live-update endpoint (SSE or equivalent) without a cookie returns 401 and closes (curl -i).
- [ ] ISC-4: Sign-in page offers email magic link and email code, the same two options AccessBuddy's `/sign-in` offers (Interceptor screenshot).
- [ ] ISC-5: Magic link email is sent via Resend and lands on `/auth/callback` which exchanges the Firebase ID token for the session cookie (Interceptor flow + Resend log).
- [ ] ISC-6: Email OTP flow (`send-otp` → `verify-otp`) issues the HMAC `webauthn.` session cookie with scrypt-hashed codes, 5-minute expiry, 5-attempt lockout (route Read + test).
- [ ] ISC-7: Session cookie attributes are `HttpOnly; Secure; SameSite=Lax; Path=/; Max-Age=1209600` (curl -i Set-Cookie).
- [ ] ISC-8: Every API route calls `getAuthUser()` before touching data (Grep: zero data routes without it).
- [ ] ISC-9: A tampered HMAC cookie (flipped signature byte) returns 401 (curl).
- [ ] ISC-10: An expired HMAC cookie returns 401 (unit test with iat/exp in the past).
- [ ] ISC-11: Logout at `DELETE /api/auth/session` (via `window.OSS_LOGOUT_URL` link) clears the cookie and the next page load redirects to sign-in (Interceptor).
- [ ] ISC-12: Rate limits on send-magic-link and send-otp are 10/IP and 5/email per 60 s, backed by `rate_limit_buckets` as in AccessBuddy (test + Read).
- [ ] ISC-13: `SESSION_SIGNING_SECRET` under 32 chars fails closed at startup (env.ts zod test).
- [ ] ISC-14: Dev login route returns 404 in production build (curl on deployed URL).
- [ ] ISC-15: `safeRedirect` rejects `//evil` and backslash redirects (unit test).

### Access control
- [ ] ISC-16: Only emails on the member allow-list can obtain a session; a non-listed email completing sign-in gets a "not a member" page and no cookie (Interceptor + curl).
- [ ] ISC-17: Allow-list is a table/collection with `email`, `displayName`, `addedBy`, `addedAt` and is editable only by an admin role (schema Read + test).
- [ ] ISC-18: Nick's email is seeded as the first admin (SELECT or doc read).
- [ ] ISC-19: An authenticated member can read and write every app collection; an authenticated non-admin cannot edit the allow-list (test 403).
- [ ] ISC-20: Anti: no route under `/lsv/dailysummary` returns any doc data to an anonymous request (curl sweep of all routes, all 401/3xx).

### Storage backend
- [ ] ISC-21: Backend technology chosen and recorded in Decisions after Nick's answer (Postgres on shared AccessBuddy instance vs Firestore vs new instance) (Read Decisions).
- [ ] ISC-22: `db.collection("units").onSnapshot(cb)` delivers `{docs:[{id,data()}]}` with all seeded units on first call (browser console assertion via Interceptor).
- [ ] ISC-23: `db.doc("config/settings").onSnapshot(cb)` delivers `{exists:true,data()}` (console assertion).
- [ ] ISC-24: `db.doc("units/SC40").set(obj)` persists and the API `GET` returns the same object (curl after set).
- [ ] ISC-25: `db.doc("events/<id>").delete()` removes the doc and subsequent snapshot omits it (console + curl).
- [ ] ISC-26: A write in browser A appears in browser B within 5 seconds without reload (two Interceptor tabs, timed).
- [ ] ISC-27: Each written doc carries `updatedBy` = signed-in user id and `updatedAt` ISO timestamp (curl GET shows fields).
- [ ] ISC-28: `window.claude.use("user").id()` is replaced by a shim returning the session user's id (Grep + console).
- [ ] ISC-29: `profiles(ids)` shim returns display names for known ids from the allow-list (console).
- [ ] ISC-30: `window.claude.use("downloads")` replaced by Blob + `<a download>` browser download; Word file saves locally (Interceptor download event).
- [ ] ISC-31: Anti: `window.claude.use("sample")` has no remaining references in `src/ux/*` or `index.html` (Grep returns 0).
- [ ] ISC-32: Settings → Download data file produces `{format:"lsv-operational-service-summary", docs:{...}}` identical in shape to the sample (JSON schema check).
- [ ] ISC-33: Settings → Open data file restores all docs from a file and they persist to the backend (Interceptor + curl).
- [ ] ISC-34: Writes are rejected with 400 when the doc path is not one of the five collections or two config docs (curl `PUT /api/docs/bogus/x`).
- [ ] ISC-35: Doc payloads over 256 KB are rejected with 413 (curl).
- [ ] ISC-36: Concurrent set on the same doc is last-write-wins with no 500s (bun test, 20 parallel writes).
- [ ] ISC-37: Anti: the browser never holds a database credential or service key (Grep built bundle for `postgres://`, `private_key`).

### Seeding
- [ ] ISC-38: Seed script loads `Operational Service Summary data 2026-11-16.json` and writes every doc under `docs` (script output count equals JSON key count).
- [ ] ISC-39: Seed is idempotent: second run changes zero docs (script reports 0 changed).
- [ ] ISC-40: After seed, unit count in the app's Services tab equals the number of `units/*` keys in the JSON (Interceptor + jq).
- [ ] ISC-41: `config/contacts` and `config/settings` present after seed (curl).

### Weather automation
- [ ] ISC-42: One-off fetch of IDV10753.xml from Cloud Run in australia-southeast1 succeeds (Cloud Run job log shows FTP 226).
- [ ] ISC-43: Weather job fetches IDV10753, IDV10752, IDV10751 over FTP with User-Agent `LSV-OSS-weather/1.0 ...` (job log lines).
- [ ] ISC-44: Job builds `lsv-bom-weather` JSON with the same keys the bookmarklet produces (bun test comparing to a saved bookmarklet output).
- [ ] ISC-45: Job applies the `BOM_FEED` area-to-town mapping and `bomFeedToGrid()` logic ported or shared from the page (test: same grid for same feed).
- [ ] ISC-46: Job writes `weather/<YYYY-MM-DD>` for today plus six days (7 docs, curl list).
- [ ] ISC-47: Each written day has `source` = `BOM forecast issued <time>` with the issue time from the feed (curl shows field).

    steps:

# Called by release-please when a release is created. Same shape as
# AccessBuddy's deploy.yml: WIF auth, build, push three tags, update the
# Cloud Run service to the sha image.
name: Deploy

on:
  workflow_call:
    inputs:
      version:
        required: true
        type: string

env:
  GCP_PROJECT_ID: lsv-oss-prod
  GCP_REGION: australia-southeast1
  CLOUD_RUN_SERVICE: lsv-oss-prod
  AR_REPO: lsv-oss
  IMAGE_NAME: app

concurrency:
  group: deploy-production
  cancel-in-progress: false

permissions:
  contents: read
  id-token: write

jobs:
  ci:
    name: CI
    uses: ./.github/workflows/ci.yml

  deploy:
    name: Deploy to Cloud Run
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: [ci]
    environment: production
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - name: Authenticate to Google Cloud
        uses: google-github-actions/auth@v2
        with:
          workload_identity_provider: ${{ secrets.GCP_WORKLOAD_IDENTITY_PROVIDER }}
          service_account: ${{ secrets.GCP_SERVICE_ACCOUNT }}

      - uses: google-github-actions/setup-gcloud@v2

      - run: gcloud auth configure-docker ${{ env.GCP_REGION }}-docker.pkg.dev --quiet

      - name: Build image
        env:
          IMAGE: ${{ env.GCP_REGION }}-docker.pkg.dev/${{ env.GCP_PROJECT_ID }}/${{ env.AR_REPO }}/${{ env.IMAGE_NAME }}
        run: |
          docker build --platform linux/amd64 \
            --build-arg NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_URL=https://nicholaswood.com.au \
            --build-arg NEXT_PUBLIC_FIREBASE_API_KEY=${{ secrets.NEXT_PUBLIC_FIREBASE_API_KEY }} \
            --build-arg NEXT_PUBLIC_FIREBASE_AUTH_DOMAIN=lsv-oss-prod.firebaseapp.com \
            --build-arg NEXT_PUBLIC_FIREBASE_PROJECT_ID=${{ env.GCP_PROJECT_ID }} \
            --build-arg NEXT_PUBLIC_FIREBASE_APP_ID=${{ secrets.NEXT_PUBLIC_FIREBASE_APP_ID }} \
            -t ${IMAGE}:${{ github.sha }} \
            -t ${IMAGE}:v${{ inputs.version }} \
            -t ${IMAGE}:latest .

      - name: Push image
        env:
          IMAGE: ${{ env.GCP_REGION }}-docker.pkg.dev/${{ env.GCP_PROJECT_ID }}/${{ env.AR_REPO }}/${{ env.IMAGE_NAME }}
        run: |
          docker push ${IMAGE}:${{ github.sha }}
          docker push ${IMAGE}:v${{ inputs.version }}
          docker push ${IMAGE}:latest

      - name: Deploy to Cloud Run
        run: |
          gcloud run services update ${{ env.CLOUD_RUN_SERVICE }} \
            --image=${{ env.GCP_REGION }}-docker.pkg.dev/${{ env.GCP_PROJECT_ID }}/${{ env.AR_REPO }}/${{ env.IMAGE_NAME }}:${{ github.sha }} \
            --region=${{ env.GCP_REGION }} \
            --project=${{ env.GCP_PROJECT_ID }}

      - name: Verify deployed version
        run: |
          sleep 10
          curl -fsS https://nicholaswood.com.au/lsv/dailysummary/api/health | tee /dev/stderr | grep -q '"version":"${{ inputs.version }}"'

input.content:
# LSV Operational Service Summary

Life Saving Victoria's Operational Service Summary tool, hosted at
`https://nicholaswood.com.au/lsv/dailysummary` behind AccessBuddy's sign-in
pattern, with Firestore for live multi-member data and a scheduled BOM
weather job.

| Piece | Where |
|---|---|
| GCP project | `lsv-oss-prod`, australia-southeast1 |
| Runtime | Cloud Run service `lsv-oss-prod` (Next.js 15, Bun image, min 0 instances) |
| Data | Firestore Native `(default)`; rules in `firestore.rules` |
| Sign-in | Firebase Auth email link (and email code when Resend is configured); 14-day httpOnly `session` cookie; member allow-list in `members/` |
| Weather | Cloud Scheduler `lsv-oss-weather-morning` 06:00 and `-afternoon` 16:30 Melbourne → `GET /api/cron/weather` (OIDC) |
| Infra | `infra/terraform` (state in `gs://lsv-oss-prod-tfstate`) |
| Deploy | GitHub Actions: `ci.yml` on every push, `release-please.yml` cuts a release and runs `deploy.yml` over Workload Identity Federation |

## The page

`oss/index.html` is the built artifact page. Edit the parts under
`oss/src/ux/` and run `python3 build.py` there to rebuild; never hand-edit the
built file. The server injects, per request, a CSP nonce on each script tag,
`window.OSS_USER_NAME`, `window.OSS_LOGOUT_URL`, `window.OSS_BOOTSTRAP`, and
`/vendor/bridge.js`, which provides `window.OSS_BACKEND` (`db`, `user`,
`downloads`, `refreshWeather`, `logout`) in place of the claude.ai
capabilities. docx, xlsx and jszip are vendored in `public/vendor` by
`bun run vendor` (hashes in `scripts/vendor.lock.json`) so the CSP is
`'self'`-only.

## Local development

```bash
bun install
cp .env.example .env            # fill the NEXT_PUBLIC_FIREBASE_* values
gcloud auth application-default login --project lsv-oss-prod
bun run vendor && bun run dev   # http://localhost:3000/lsv/dailysummary
```

Add yourself to the allow-list once (or use the seed `--admin` flag):

```bash
bun run seed path/to/data.json --admin you@example.com "Your Name"
```

## Deploy

A deploy is a release. Merge conventional-commit PRs to `main`; release-please
opens a release PR; merging it creates the release and `deploy.yml` builds,
pushes `:sha`, `:vX.Y.Z` and `:latest` to Artifact Registry, updates the Cloud
Run service and checks `/api/health` reports the new version.

After merging a release PR, do not merge anything else to `main` until
"Deploy to Cloud Run" is green. If a later push cancels the release run,
`gh run rerun <run-id> --failed` re-runs the deploy for that release.

GitHub repository secrets (values from `terraform output`):
`GCP_WORKLOAD_IDENTITY_PROVIDER`, `GCP_SERVICE_ACCOUNT`,
`NEXT_PUBLIC_FIREBASE_API_KEY`, `NEXT_PUBLIC_FIREBASE_APP_ID`.

Manual deploy from a laptop (emergency only):

```bash
IMG=australia-southeast1-docker.pkg.dev/lsv-oss-prod/lsv-oss/app:manual-$(date +%Y%m%d%H%M)
docker build --platform linux/amd64 --build-arg NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_URL=https://nicholaswood.com.au \
  --build-arg NEXT_PUBLIC_FIREBASE_API_KEY=... --build-arg NEXT_PUBLIC_FIREBASE_AUTH_DOMAIN=lsv-oss-prod.firebaseapp.com \
  --build-arg NEXT_PUBLIC_FIREBASE_PROJECT_ID=lsv-oss-prod --build-arg NEXT_PUBLIC_FIREBASE_APP_ID=... -t $IMG .
docker push $IMG
gcloud run services update lsv-oss-prod --image=$IMG --region=australia-southeast1 --project=lsv-oss-prod
```

## Rollback

Cloud Run keeps every revision. Send traffic back to the previous one:

```bash
gcloud run revisions list --service=lsv-oss-prod --region=australia-southeast1 --project=lsv-oss-prod
gcloud run services update-traffic lsv-oss-prod --to-revisions=<previous-revision>=100 \
  --region=australia-southeast1 --project=lsv-oss-prod
```

Rolling back code does not roll back data. Firestore has no schema
migrations in this app, so older revisions read current data fine.

## Infrastructure changes

```bash
cd infra/terraform
terraform init -backend-config="bucket=lsv-oss-prod-tfstate"
terraform plan -var-file=prod.tfvars
terraform apply -var-file=prod.tfvars
```

`prod.tfvars` is gitignored. Firestore rules deploy with Terraform
(`google_firebaserules_release`), so a rules change is a Terraform apply.

Domain: Cloud Run domain mapping on `nicholaswood.com.au` (Google-managed
TLS). One-off steps the account owner does: verify the domain
(`gcloud domains verify nicholaswood.com.au`), create the mapping
(`gcloud beta run domain-mappings create --service lsv-oss-prod --domain nicholaswood.com.au --region australia-southeast1`),
copy the A/AAAA records it prints into `cloud_run_domain_ipv4/6` in
`prod.tfvars`, apply, and point GoDaddy's nameservers at the Cloud DNS
`dns_name_servers` output.

## Weather job

Runs 06:00 and 16:30 Melbourne via Cloud Scheduler. It fetches
`IDV10753.xml`, `IDV10752.xml` and `IDV10751.xml` over the BOM's anonymous FTP,
projects towns onto areas (`src/lib/weather/mapping.ts`, the server twin of the
page's `BOM_FEED`), and writes `weather/<YYYY-MM-DD>` for seven days with
`source: "BOM forecast issued <time>"`. Cells listed in a day's `manual` array
(`"<area>|<field>"`) were typed by a member and are never overwritten. Status
is in `config/weatherStatus` (last run, last issued, last error).

Rerun it:

```bash
# From the UI: Weather tab → Refresh from BOM now (session-gated, 2/min).
# From Scheduler:
gcloud scheduler jobs run lsv-oss-weather-morning --location=australia-southeast1 --project=lsv-oss-prod
# From a laptop with ADC:
bun run weather            # writes
bun run weather --dry-run  # prints the grid, no writes
```

Logs: `gcloud logging read 'resource.type=cloud_run_revision AND textPayload:"[weather]"' --project=lsv-oss-prod --limit=20`.

BOM licence: anonymous FTP data is for internal organisational use. The site
stays behind sign-in; nothing from the feeds is served to anonymous requests.

## Backup and restore

Members: Settings → Download data file produces
`{ format: "lsv-operational-service-summary", docs: {...} }`; Settings → Open
data file writes it back through the signed-in session.

Ops restore from a file (idempotent; `--replace` also deletes docs not in the file):

```bash
bun run seed "Operational Service Summary data 2026-11-16.json"
bun run seed backup.json --replace
```

Point-in-time export for safekeeping:

```bash
gcloud firestore export gs://lsv-oss-prod-tfstate/firestore-export/$(date +%F) --project=lsv-oss-prod
```

## Members

Allow-list docs live in `members/<email>` with `displayName` and `role`
(`member` or `admin`). Add or change via the API as an admin:

```bash
curl -X PUT https://nicholaswood.com.au/lsv/dailysummary/api/members \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -b 'session=...' \
  -d '{"email":"person@lsv.com.au","displayName":"First Last","role":"member"}'
```

or with the seed script's `--admin` flag for the first admin. Removing a member
revokes their Firebase refresh tokens, so open tabs lose data access within an
hour and the next page load is refused.

## Rules

- Never call LIMSOC production. Unit data came from staging only.
- Wording: members, not staff. `unit.area` is Region (Central/East/West);
  `unit.regionName` is Area (Bass, Port Phillip, Kingston, ...).
- Costs: everything here sits in GCP free tiers except the Cloud DNS zone
  (about US$0.20 a month). No Cloud SQL, no load balancer, min instances 0.

input.content:
---
name: gotcha-check-registry-delegation-before-dns-changes
description: Before deleting a DNS zone or telling Nick where to add records, read the delegation at the TLD servers, not a cached resolver answer
metadata:
  type: feedback
---

Before deleting a DNS zone, or telling Nick which DNS host to add a record at, query the registry's own servers for the delegation: `dig +norec NS <domain> @$(dig +short NS com.au | head -1)`. A plain `dig NS` can show stale cached nameservers for an hour or more.

**Why:** On 22 Nov 2026 I took nicholaswood.com.au offline for public lookups. Nick had switched the registry nameservers to Google (`ns-cloud-d1..d4`) on my earlier instruction; my resolver still showed GoDaddy's, so I told him DNS was staying at GoDaddy, had him add a CNAME there, and deleted the Cloud DNS zone. Every public resolver then returned SERVFAIL (EDE 22, no reachable authority). Recreating the zone did not fix it, because Cloud DNS assigned a different nameserver shard (`b`, not `d`).

**How to apply:** Check delegation at the TLD first. Treat a Cloud DNS zone that a registry delegates to as undeletable (`prevent_destroy`); a recreated zone gets a new shard and needs a registrar change. Related: [[project-lsv-service-summary]].

input.summary: Ack migration; flag hostname vs app id
input.message:
Service Summary migration acknowledged and started in my thread (brief, DEPLOY.md and the skill read); one platform question blocks nothing yet but needs your answer: the hostname label differs from the app id.
Nick's decisions give app id `oss` but hostname `service-summary.poc.nicholaswood.com.au`. `modules/poc-app` derives the hostname as `<app_id>.<poc_domain>`, so as written it would create `oss.poc.nicholaswood.com.au`. My plan: in my vendored copy of the module add an optional `hostname_label` variable (default = app_id) used only for `local.hostname`; every other name stays derived from `oss`. That needs the platform side to treat the app's host as `service-summary.poc.nicholaswood.com.au`: the sign-in authorised domain (if you add per-POC domains from the `pocs` map rather than a wildcard), the hub registry URL for `oss`, and `APP_URL` in live-e2e. Tell me if you would rather carry `hostname_label` in the platform module itself (I will then vendor that version), or if anything on your side assumes host == id.
Other choices I am making, say if any conflicts with the platform: (1) the app moves to the root of its hostname (no `/lsv/dailysummary` prefix) so `/api/health`, `/sign-in` and `/api/jobs/<name>` match the module and live-e2e; (2) the browser keeps the member's own Firebase session for Firestore, with a server-minted custom token only as fallback, role copied from the gate-verified session; (3) the rules I will send you make revokes immediate in the browser too, by checking `platformAccess/$(request.auth.uid)` in rules (lower-only, same as the gate), so please confirm the hub writes that doc with `role: null` on revoke and the role on grant/downgrade; (4) display names: I will keep a server-written `profiles/<uid>` {name,email} in `poc-oss` since `members/` is retired. I will message you when the rules file is ready and when I am ready for allocations and registration.

input.content:
# LSV Operational Service Summary

Life Saving Victoria's Operational Service Summary tool, a tenant of the LSV
POC platform (app id `oss`), served at
`https://service-summary.poc.nicholaswood.com.au` behind the platform's
sign-in, with Firestore for live multi-member data and a scheduled BOM weather
job.

| Piece | Where |
|---|---|
| GCP project | `lsv-poc` (shared with the other LSV POCs), australia-southeast1 |
| Runtime | Cloud Run service `poc-oss` (Next.js 15, Bun image, scales to zero) |
| Data | Firestore named database `poc-oss`; rules in `firestore.rules`, released by the platform |
| Sign-in | Shared LSV POC sign-in pool, email link only. The hub (https://poc.nicholaswood.com.au) allocates who may open the app and issues the claim `poc_oss` = `member` or `admin`. 14-day httpOnly `__session` cookie signed by this app |
| Front door | Firebase Hosting site `lsv-poc-oss`, hostname in the delegated `poc` sub-zone |
| Weather | Cloud Scheduler `oss-weather-morning` 06:00 and `oss-weather-afternoon` 16:30 Melbourne → `POST /api/jobs/weather` (Google-signed token) |
| Infra | `infra/` calls the vendored `infra/modules/poc-app`; state in `gs://lsv-poc-tfstate`, prefix `apps/oss` |
| Deploy | GitHub Actions: `ci.yml` on pull requests, `deploy.yml` on every push to `main` over Workload Identity Federation |

The platform repo is `nicholas-wood/lsv-poc-platform`. Two parts of it are
vendored here and must not be edited in place: `vendor/poc-auth` (sign-in) and
`infra/modules/poc-app` (Terraform). `vendor/PLATFORM_COMMIT` records the
commit they were copied from; to update, re-copy both and bump that file.

## Who can get in

Access is not managed in this app. The platform owner allocates it per person
in the hub. This app:

- verifies the sign-in token with Google's public keys and reads only the
  `poc_oss` claim; a claim for another POC, or a bare `member` claim, grants
  nothing;
- never writes sign-in claims and holds no Firebase Auth admin permission;
- honours a revoke or downgrade at once: the hub writes
  `platformAccess/<uid>` into this app's database, the server checks it on
  every request (15 second cache) and the Firestore rules check it on every
  read and write.

A member's display name is kept in `profiles/<uid>`, written by the server at
sign-in.

## The page

`oss/index.html` is the built page (an HTML fragment; the server adds the
document shell). Edit the parts under `oss/src/ux/` and run
`bun run build:page`; never hand-edit the built file. `oss/src` is the
original pack's `src` folder with the hosting changes applied: vendored
library tags in `build.py`, the hosted backend boot and "Refresh from BOM now"
in `wiring.js` and `markup.html`, and per-cell `manual` tracking in `views.js`
and `import.js`. `oss/samples/` (data file and OSSD spreadsheet) is gitignored
because it holds operational contacts.

Per request the server (`src/app/route.ts`) injects a CSP nonce on each script
tag, `window.OSS_USER_NAME`, `window.OSS_LOGOUT_URL`, `window.OSS_BOOTSTRAP`,
and `/vendor/bridge.js`, which provides `window.OSS_BACKEND` (`db`, `user`,
`downloads`, `refreshWeather`, `logout`) in place of the claude.ai
capabilities. docx, xlsx and jszip are vendored in `public/vendor` by
`bun run vendor` (hashes in `scripts/vendor.lock.json`). The browser reads and
writes Firestore directly with the member's own Firebase session; if the
browser has none, the server mints a token from the verified session.

## Local development

```bash
bun install
cp .env.example .env            # fill NEXT_PUBLIC_FIREBASE_API_KEY and SESSION_SIGNING_SECRET
gcloud auth application-default login --project lsv-poc
bun run vendor && bun run dev   # http://localhost:3000
```

The browser API key only answers from `poc.nicholaswood.com.au` hostnames, so
sign-in does not complete from localhost. Use the probes against the deployed
app for anything that needs a session.

## Deploy

A deploy is a push to `main`: CI (secret scan, typecheck, tests, dependency
audit, build), then the image is built, pushed and released, and
`/api/health` must report the new commit. Only conventional commits to `main`
deploy. The deploy identity admits only this repository on `refs/heads/main`.

Repository settings: environment `production`; variable `FIREBASE_API_KEY`
(the platform's public web API key).

## Rollback

Cloud Run keeps every revision:

```bash
gcloud run revisions list --service=poc-oss --region=australia-southeast1 --project=lsv-poc
gcloud run services update-traffic poc-oss --to-revisions=<previous-revision>=100 \
  --region=australia-southeast1 --project=lsv-poc
```

Rolling back code does not roll back data. There are no schema migrations, so
older revisions read current data.

## Infrastructure changes

```bash
cd infra
terraform init -backend-config="bucket=lsv-poc-tfstate" -backend-config="prefix=apps/oss"
terraform plan -var-file=app.tfvars -out=tfplan
terraform apply tfplan
```

`app.tfvars` is gitignored; start from `example.tfvars`. Apply the saved plan
as a whole, never a targeted Cloud Run resource. Firestore rules are not
applied from here: send `firestore.rules` to the platform, which reviews it
into `terraform/platform/rules/oss.rules` and releases it.

Never delete or recreate a DNS zone that something delegates to. The parent
zone `nicholaswood.com.au` lives in project `lsv-oss-prod` and stays there.

## Weather job

Runs 06:00 and 16:30 Melbourne. It fetches `IDV10753.xml`, `IDV10752.xml` and
`IDV10751.xml` over the BOM's anonymous FTP, builds the same `lsv-bom-weather`
feed the bookmarklet builds, projects it onto the areas in `config/settings`
(`src/lib/weather/mapping.ts` is a line-for-line port of the page's `BOM_FEED`
and `bomFeedToGrid()`), and writes `weather/<YYYY-MM-DD>` for seven days with
`source: "BOM forecast issued <time>"`. Cells listed in a day's `manual` array
(`"<area>|<field>"`) were typed by a member and are never overwritten; the
page adds a key when a member edits a cell and removes it when the cell is
cleared or filled from the BOM. Days saved before tracking existed, and not
sourced from a BOM feed, count as wholly typed. Status is in
`config/weatherStatus`.

Rerun it:

```bash
# From the UI: Weather tab → Refresh from BOM now (member session, 2 a minute).
gcloud scheduler jobs run oss-weather-morning --location=australia-southeast1 --project=lsv-poc
# From a laptop with application-default credentials:
FIRESTORE_DATABASE=poc-oss FIREBASE_PROJECT_ID=lsv-poc bun run weather
bun run weather --dry-run <data-file.json>   # prints the grid, no writes
```

Logs: `gcloud logging read 'resource.labels.service_name="poc-oss" AND textPayload:"[weather]"' --project=lsv-poc --limit=20`.

BOM licence: anonymous FTP data is for internal organisational use. The site
stays behind sign-in; nothing from the feeds is served to anonymous requests.

## Backup and restore

Members: Settings → Download data file produces
`{ format: "lsv-operational-service-summary", docs: {...} }`; Settings → Open
data file writes it back through the signed-in session.

Ops restore from a file (idempotent; `--replace` also deletes app documents
that are not in the file):

```bash
bun run seed "Operational Service Summary data 2026-11-16.json"
bun run seed backup.json --replace
```

## Probes

Run as the platform owner on a machine with `gcloud` application-default
credentials (they mint test sign-ins; see `scripts/lib-probe.ts`):

```bash
export APP_URL=https://service-summary.poc.nicholaswood.com.au NEXT_PUBLIC_FIREBASE_API_KEY=<key>
bun run probe <allocated-email> <unallocated-email>     # HTTP surface
bun run scripts/rules-probe.ts                          # Firestore rules, including revoke and bare claims
bun run scripts/browser-probe.ts <allocated-email> "<ossd.xlsx>"   # two real browsers; writes test data
```

## Rules

- Never call LIMSOC production. Unit data came from staging only.
- Wording: members, not staff. `unit.area` is Region (Central/East/West);
  `unit.regionName` is Area (Bass, Port Phillip, Kingston, ...).
- Costs: everything sits in free tiers at this use; the platform's budget
  alert covers the shared project.

Rules stand as reviewed, and one defect in `modules/poc-app` for you to fix upstream: the job-failure alert is rejected for any POC with scheduled jobs.

When you carry the fix in the platform module I will re-vendor and drop the note.
